items.title: fix(body): clean up cancelled request streams
items.body:
`getRequestWebStream()`'s Node fallback adds `data`/`end`/`error` listeners to `event.node.req` when the stream is created and never removes them. If the stream is cancelled while the client is still sending, the next chunk calls `controller.enqueue()` on a closed stream and throws `TypeError [ERR_INVALID_STATE]: Invalid state: Controller is already closed` outside any handler. It also enqueues every chunk regardless of demand, so a fast upload is buffered in memory while the handler is busy.

This makes the bridge lazy and pull-based. The stream uses `highWaterMark: 0`; a Web stream that is never read doesn't touch the request, so Node's own drain and `readRawBody()` behave as before. No new imports.

- The first `pull()` checks the request first: an errored request rejects with its error; if the response already finished while the upload was incomplete, it rejects with `Response already finished`; an ended request closes; a destroyed one rejects with an `aborted` error (`ECONNRESET`). Otherwise it attaches the listeners and resumes the request. A request that closes later without `end` or `error` rejects a pending read with the same `aborted` error.
- Each chunk is enqueued and the request is paused again unless another read is already waiting (`enqueue()` can call `pull()` synchronously for it).
- `cancel()` removes the listeners and resumes the request, so the rest of the upload drains and the handler can still respond (e.g. 413).
- When the response finishes, the listeners are removed and the request is resumed, so a handler that read part of the body and returned without cancelling doesn't leave the upload paused on a keep-alive socket. A read still pending at that point, or any later one, rejects with `Response already finished` rather than hanging or ending as if the upload were complete.

Tests (`test/body.test.ts`): cancel then keep sending, then respond (no uncaught error, listeners released, response delivered), also with the upload still open; an unread 8 MiB body stays bounded after one read; two concurrent reads; a request that ended or was aborted before the first read; a first read after the response finished; a request closed without an error while a read is pending; a pending read when the response finishes; keep-alive reuse after an unused Web body, after `toWebRequest()` + `readRawBody()`, and after a partial Web body read. `pnpm test` (369) and `pnpm build` pass.

items.title: fix(response): run sync onResponse before returning the response
items.body:
Resolves #1647

## Summary

Invoke `config.onResponse` synchronously inside `toResponse()` once `prepareResponse()` has produced a resolved `Response`, and only allocate the promise chain when `onResponse` returns a thenable. Dispose observation is extracted to a module-level `observeDispose()` helper so neither the no-hook path nor the sync-hook path allocates per-request closures.

```diff
 toResponse(val, event, config)
   prepareResponse(val, event, config) -> Response
   if config.onResponse
-    Promise.resolve()
-      .then(() => onResponse(response, event))
-      .catch(logError)
-      .then(() => dispose?.observe(response, val) ?? response)
+    try
+      hookRes = onResponse(response, event)
+      if typeof hookRes?.then === "function"
+        return Promise.resolve(hookRes)
+          .catch(logError)
+          .then(() => observeDispose(event, response, val))
+    catch (error)
+      logError(error)
+  return observeDispose(event, response, val)
```

- Reading `hookRes?.then` inside the `try` block ensures a custom object with a throwing `.then` getter is absorbed and logged the same way as a synchronous throw, while `Promise.resolve(hookRes)` adopts custom thenables whose `.then` throws on invocation or second read.
- Adjusts bundle ceilings in `test/bench/bundle.test.ts` to match measured sizes (`H3Core`: `7952 B` / `3170 B gzip`, `defineHandler`: `7144 B` / `2903 B gzip`; `defineHandler` on `main` was already `7045 B` / `2872 B gzip` over the prior `7040` / `2870` budget).

## Evidence

- **Before:** With a synchronous handler and synchronous `onResponse`, `app.fetch()` returned a `Promise<Response>` and queued three promise reactions per request; `onResponse` ran a microtask after `fetch()` returned.
- **After:** `app.fetch()` returns a plain `Response` synchronously (`0` `PROMISE` allocations on warmup `fetch` loops), `onResponse` runs before `fetch()` returns, sync throws and throwing/rejecting thenables are absorbed without invoking `onError` or skipping `onDispose`, and `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm build`, and `pnpm vitest --run` pass (`75` files, `3355` passed).

## Merge Danger

**Door:** Two-way

Isolated to `toResponse()` in `src/response.ts` plus unit tests and bundle ceilings.

**Blast Radius:** Narrow

`toResponse()` and `app.fetch()` are already typed `Response | Promise<Response>` (and already returned a plain `Response` when `onResponse` was unset). Direct JS callers chaining `app.fetch(...).then(...)` without `await` or `Promise.resolve(...)` when both the handler and `onResponse` are synchronous now receive a `Response` directly, as noted in #1647.

items.title: fix(static): evaluate `If-Match` and `If-Unmodified-Since` preconditions
items.body:
Resolves #1639.

`serveStatic` now evaluates `If-Match` and `If-Unmodified-Since` before the existing `If-None-Match` / `If-Modified-Since` check, as RFC 9110 §13.2.2 orders them, and responds `412 Precondition Failed` when they fail:

- `If-Match` uses strong comparison: `*` passes, a weak ETag never matches, and a missing ETag fails.
- `If-Unmodified-Since` is only evaluated when `If-Match` is absent; an invalid date is ignored.

The check lives next to `isCacheMatch` in `src/utils/internal/cache.ts` as `isPreconditionFailed()`. Tests in `test/static.test.ts` (node and web) cover each case; they fail on main and pass with the change. `pnpm lint` and `pnpm typecheck` pass. In the full `pnpm vitest run`, only `test/bench/bundle.test.ts` (defineHandler bundle 7045 > 7040) fails, and it fails the same way on main locally.

Not included: the `cache-control: no-store` header nitro adds on its 412, since h3 error responses don't carry headers set on `event.res`.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Static file requests now return a precondition failure when `If-Match` or `If-Unmodified-Since` conditions are not met, rather than returning a cached response. When both conditions are provided, `If-Match` takes precedence. Invalid date values are ignored.
* **Tests**
  * Added coverage for ETag and date-based preconditions, including wildcard and list matching, condition precedence, supported date formats, and invalid dates.
